issues.legal_issue: Any defendant in a suit for specific performance may contest whether the plaintiff has met the requirement of readiness and willingness to perform the contract.
material_facts: The suit sought specific performance of an agreement to sell.
The plaintiff had not initially pleaded readiness and willingness, but later added that plea by amendment.
The defendants were subsequent purchasers of the property and sought to contend that the plaintiff and her legal representatives had not been ready and willing to perform the agreement.
The lower courts declined to permit that contention, relying on the rule that the plea was available only to the vendor or the vendor’s legal representatives.
issues.conclusion: The contention was available to the subsequent-purchaser defendants, and the court had to determine whether the plaintiff had averred and proved performance or continuous readiness and willingness. The decision limiting the plea to the vendor was erroneous. The appeal was allowed, the judgments below were set aside, and the suit was remanded for that determination.
issues.legal_principle: Section 16(c) of the Specific Relief Act bars specific performance where the plaintiff fails to aver and prove performance or continuous readiness and willingness to perform the essential terms of the contract, except where performance was prevented or waived by the defendant. The obligation is on the court to withhold specific performance if the requirement is not met; any defendant may raise the issue. This accords with Ardeshir H. Mama v. Flora Sassoon and Gomathinayagam Pillai v. Palaniswami Nadar, and the contrary limitation stated in Jugraj Singh v. Labh Singh was erroneous. Lakhi Ram v. Trikha Ram had doubted that limitation but was decided on another point.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The claimant seeks a decree compelling performance of a contract.
predicates.defendant_contests_plaintiff_readiness: A defendant disputes that the claimant performed or was ready and willing to perform the claimant’s contractual obligations.

issues.definition: When a defendant contests the claimant’s readiness in a specific-performance suit, the court must determine whether the claimant was ready and willing to perform.
